title.en: Plot z on the Argand plane

say.en: Every complex number a plus ib is a point (a, b) on a plane. Its distance from the origin is its modulus. In this lesson: Plot z on the Argand plane.
Find the argument.
Write z in polar form.

body.en: Plot $z = x + iy$ as the point $P(x, y)$. The x-axis is the real axis and the y-axis the imaginary axis. $|z| = OP$, the distance from the origin. $\bar{z} = x - iy$ is the mirror image of $z$ in the real axis.
body.kn: ಆರ್ಗಂಡ್ ಸಮತಲದಲ್ಲಿ z = x + iy ಬಿಂದು (x, y). x-ಅಕ್ಷ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷ, y-ಅಕ್ಷ ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಅಕ್ಷ. z̄ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ z ನ ಪ್ರತಿಬಿಂಬ.

points.en: z̄: reflection in the real axis

narration.en: On the Argand plane the real part is the x-coordinate and the imaginary part is the y-coordinate. The modulus is the distance from the origin, and the conjugate is the reflection in the real axis.
narration.kn: ಆರ್ಗಂಡ್ ಸಮತಲದಲ್ಲಿ z = x + iy ಬಿಂದು (x, y). x-ಅಕ್ಷ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷ, y-ಅಕ್ಷ ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಅಕ್ಷ. z̄ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷದಲ್ಲಿ z ನ ಪ್ರತಿಬಿಂಬ.

r is the length OP: root of 1 plus 3, which is 2.
Theta is measured from the positive real axis: here 120 degrees, or 2 pi by 3.
So z = 2 times cos 120 degrees plus i sin 120 degrees.
The principal argument always lies between minus pi and pi.

narration.en: Drag z = x + iy. Its distance from O is r = |z| and its angle with the positive real axis is the argument θ, taken in (−180°, 180°]. Rotating by α multiplies z by cos α + i sin α.
narration.kn: z = x + iy ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. O ಯಿಂದ ದೂರ r = |z|, ಧನ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷದೊಂದಿಗಿನ ಕೋನ ಕೋನಾಂಕ θ, (−180°, 180°] ನಲ್ಲಿ. α ತಿರುಗುವಿಕೆ z ಅನ್ನು cos α + i sin α ಇಂದ ಗುಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Drag z equals x plus iy. Its distance from O is r = |z| and its angle with the positive real axis is the argument theta, taken in (minus 180 degrees, 180 degrees]. Rotating by alpha multiplies z by cos alpha plus i sin alpha.
say.kn: z equals x plus iy ಎಳೆಯಿರಿ. O ಯಿಂದ ದೂರ r = |z|, ಧನ ವಾಸ್ತವ ಅಕ್ಷದೊಂದಿಗಿನ ಕೋನ ಕೋನಾಂಕ theta, (minus 180 degrees, 180 degrees] ನಲ್ಲಿ. alpha ತಿರುಗುವಿಕೆ z ಅನ್ನು cos alpha plus i sin alpha ಇಂದ ಗುಣಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: With $r = |z|$ and $\theta$ the angle $OP$ makes with the positive real axis, $x = r\cos\theta$, $y = r\sin\theta$, so $z = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)$. $\theta$ is the *argument*; the principal argument lies in $(-\pi, \pi]$. Find the acute angle $\alpha$ with $\tan\alpha = |y/x|$, then place it in the right quadrant: $\alpha$, $\pi - \alpha$, $-(\pi - \alpha)$ or $-\alpha$.
body.kn: ಧ್ರುವೀಯ ರೂಪ z = r(cos θ + i sin θ), r = |z|. ಮುಖ್ಯ ಕೋನಾಂಕ (−π, π] ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ; ಚತುರ್ಥಕ ನೋಡಿ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ.

points.en: Quadrant I: α; II: π − α

narration.en: In polar form, z equals r times cos theta plus i sin theta. Find the acute angle from tan alpha equals y over x, then adjust it for the quadrant to get the principal argument between minus pi and pi.

say.kn: ಧ್ರುವೀಯ ರೂಪ z equals r(cos theta plus i sin theta), r = |z|. ಮುಖ್ಯ ಕೋನಾಂಕ (- pi, pi ] ಅಂತರದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ; ಚತುರ್ಥಕ ನೋಡಿ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ.

say.en: Quadrant III: -(pi - alpha); IV: - alpha.

say.en: Polar form: choose the modulus r and the argument theta. The arrow is z equals r(cos theta plus i sin theta).

problem.en: Write z = 1 + i√3 in polar form.

steps.en: cos θ = 1/2, sin θ = √3/2, so θ = π/3 (first quadrant).

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Write z = 1 + i√3 in polar form.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Write z equals 1 plus i the square root of 3 in polar form.
r equals the square root of 1 plus 3 equals 2.
cos theta equals 1 over 2, sin theta equals the square root of 3 over 2, so theta equals pi /3 first quadrant.
z equals 2(cos pi /3 plus i sin pi /3).
So the answer is 2(cos pi /3 plus i sin pi /3).

problem.en: Find the modulus and principal argument of −1 − i√3.

steps.en: Point (−1, −√3) is in quadrant III; tan α = √3 gives α = π/3.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the modulus and principal argument of −1 − i√3.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the modulus and principal argument of minus 1 - i the square root of 3.
r equals the square root of 1 plus 3 equals 2.
Point (minus 1, - the square root of 3) is in quadrant III; tan alpha equals the square root of 3 gives alpha equals pi /3.
Principal argument equals -(pi - pi /3) equals minus 2 pi /3.
So the answer is Modulus 2, argument minus 2 pi /3.
